Primary focus on SDK compatibility (Python/JS), LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy placement, rate limit profiles, quotas, and observability hooks. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-19 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM); Michael Chen (CTO, Montage), Sara Ortiz (Lead ML Engineer), David Park (Platform Eng), Lena Kim (Product)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Priya, our SE, and Maya from customer success. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Michael Chen: Doing well, Jordan. Thanks. Quick note, we're short on time so we'd like to focus on integration questions — SDKs, LangChain adapters, and how rate limits would affect our gateway.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Totally, we'll keep it focused. Priya, want to kick off on the technical side?
[00:22] Priya Raman: Sure. Quick context check — Michael, Sara, David, are you evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? Any leaning today?
[00:31] Sara Ortiz: We're leaning Dedicated given PCI-type workloads. We need predictable latency and isolation. But we also want to prototype quickly so Hosted for an initial POC could work if network and data residency are OK.
[00:45] David Park: Also need to understand how Redwood would fit with our existing API gateway and service mesh — we can't rewrite the whole infra. We're thinking an outbound proxy to Redwood or an egress VPC peering.
[00:58] Priya Raman: That's helpful. On the SDK side we provide official Python and Node SDKs, and REST endpoints. For LangChain and LlamaIndex, we have maintained connectors — they map to our chat/generation and embeddings endpoints with minimal adapter code.
[01:14] Sara Ortiz: When you say connectors, is that a pip package or code snippets? How mature are they?
[01:19] Priya Raman: We publish pip/npm packages for the adapters and example notebooks. They support the standard LangChain LLM interface and LlamaIndex Retriever patterns. They also include example batching logic and best-practice prompt templates we've used in customer POCs. Maturity is high — several fintech customers use them in staging.
[01:34] Lena Kim: Any differences between using the adapter with Hosted vs Dedicated? For example, auth flows and token rotation?
[01:40] Priya Raman: Good question. Auth is the same API key model for Hosted. For Dedicated we support customer-managed API keys plus optional integration with your identity provider for per-team tokens. For Private deployments you can integrate with your KMS/HSM and SSO. Token rotation and short-lived tokens are supported via our control plane APIs.
[01:54] Michael Chen: How would we route calls? We have an existing Kong gateway and envoy sidecars. Can requests go through our gateway to Redwood, or do we need to set up a proxy in cloud?
[02:05] Priya Raman: Both patterns are supported. Common approach: keep your gateway as the single point of ingress, and configure it to forward inference requests to Redwood endpoints. With Dedicated/Private, you can also set up a private peering/VPC endpoint and route internal traffic without traversing public internet. For sidecars, continuous streaming and connection re-use is supported; we recommend connection pooling at the gateway to avoid per-request TLS overhead.
[02:28] David Park: Rate limiting — we already have per-tenant quotas in Kong. How would Redwood's rate limits interact? Do you expose headers for usage so we can reconcile?
[02:38] Priya Raman: Yes. We surface usage headers on responses (tokens consumed, request cost estimate) and you can also ingest observability hooks. On Dedicated, you can define per-customer rate limits in the Redwood config so we can enforce upstream. For Hosted, we enforce per-account quotas and provide webhook events for quota breaches. We can integrate with your quota service via webhooks or export metrics to Prometheus.
[03:00] Sara Ortiz: Can those headers be customized? We have an automated billing job that expects certain fields.
[03:06] Priya Raman: We have a default header set but we can add custom metadata via request metadata fields. For deeper billing integration we'd typically add a tiny adapter service that translates our headers to your billing format — we can include that as part of a POC.
[03:18] Jordan Lee: On observability — what would Montage get out of the box?
[03:22] Priya Raman: Per-route latency percentiles, per-model token-level costs, tracing IDs that can be propagated (traceparent), and structured logs. We support exporting to Datadog, New Relic, and self-hosted Prometheus + Grafana. Also audit logs for Private/Dedicated for compliance.
[03:37] Michael Chen: For compliance we need SOC2-level audit logs and full request/response redaction options. Is that possible?
[03:43] Maya Chen: Yes — for Dedicated/Private we can enable detailed audit logs and support field-level redaction. We also integrate with KMS for encryption at rest. We will share the SOC 2 and ISO docs after the call.
[03:55] David Park: Latency — our SLA is tight: 99th percentile under 300ms for short prompts (~128 tokens). Do you have benchmarks?
[04:03] Priya Raman: We have verified profiles per model and hardware. For a 128-token short prompt on Dedicated (A100 class equivalent) we typically see p50 ~40ms, p95 ~120ms, p99 ~260-320ms depending on batching. We'll run a focused benchmark with your traffic shape in the SE deep dive to confirm. For Hosted we provide published latency profiles but Dedicated gives more predictable tails.
[04:25] Sara Ortiz: About batching — we are sensitive to tail latency, so we want minimal batching for interactive tasks. Can you tune batching per route?
[04:32] Priya Raman: Absolutely. Batching is configurable per route; you can set max batch size, max wait, and preferential routing to low-latency instances. We also support heterogeneous pools — low-latency small-batch nodes and high-throughput batch nodes.
[04:47] Lena Kim: For LangChain / LlamaIndex ingestion, do you recommend embeddings on Hosted or Dedicated? We plan to store vectors in our managed Pinecone cluster today.
[04:56] Priya Raman: Embeddings are a high-throughput pattern; if you need predictable throughput and network locality, Dedicated with peering to your vector DB is recommended. Hosted is fine for prototypes. Our SDKs include async batch embedding helpers that work well with LlamaIndex wrappers.
[05:10] Michael Chen: Security detail: KMS — can Redwood use our AWS KMS keys?
[05:14] Priya Raman: Yes for Dedicated and Private we support BYOK via AWS KMS and also support GCP KMS or Vault. For Hosted we manage keys but can do a dedicated customer key if needed on an enterprise contract.
[05:26] David Park: Observability hooks — you mentioned Prometheus metrics. Can we get per-tenant metrics exported so we can attach to our internal dashboards?
[05:33] Priya Raman: On Dedicated we can export per-tenant metrics to your Prometheus collector via a push gateway or by allowing your scrape to our metrics endpoint over the peering link. For Hosted we provide multi-tenant metrics in the console and export aggregated metrics; detailed per-tenant Prometheus export is an enterprise feature.
[05:50] Jordan Lee: Any concerns from your side on SDK support or adapters?
[05:53] Sara Ortiz: One thing — we're heavy on asyncio and have a custom rate-limiter. Will your Python SDK play nicely with our async pipeline?
[06:02] Priya Raman: Yes, our Python SDK has both sync and async clients, and we have examples integrating with asyncio and async queue patterns. We also provide a middleware hook so you can plug in your rate-limiter before requests hit the network.
[06:16] Michael Chen: On pricing and quotas — we need a predictable monthly cap for the Dedicated plan and also the ability to burst. How does billing for burst capacity work?
[06:23] Jordan Lee: Typically Dedicated is a reserved capacity monthly commit with an overage rate for burst. There are options for burst credits or time-limited burst pools. We'll include those SKUs in the pricing doc.
[06:34] Lena Kim: If we start with Hosted for POC and then migrate to Dedicated, how seamless is it?
[06:40] Priya Raman: The API and SDKs are the same so code changes are minimal. There are some operational shifts for auth and network (peering vs public endpoints). We have a migration checklist we can share.
[06:51] David Park: One operational ask — can we place a proxy inside our VPC that rewrites headers and injects tenant metadata?
[06:58] Priya Raman: Yes, that's standard. Many customers run a lightweight proxy that enriches requests with tenant-id and tracing info. For Dedicated we can also support MTLS between your proxy and our ingress for stronger identity.
[07:10] Sara Ortiz: Regarding LlamaIndex, we currently use the Node bindings in a microservice. Do you support JS adapters and examples for vector retrieval + generation pipelines?
[07:18] Priya Raman: Yes, Node adapters exist and we have example microservice patterns showing retrieval-augmented generation with LlamaIndex + LangChain. We'll attach the repo links in the follow-up.
[07:30] Michael Chen: Any deal-breakers we should know about? E.g., data residency or audit constraints that would force us away from Hosted?
[07:36] Maya Chen: If strict data residency and customer-managed keys are required (and no external network egress allowed), Hosted may not be suitable; Dedicated or Private would be the right fit. We'll map your regulatory constraints in the next call.
[07:49] Jordan Lee: Great. To wrap, we'll do a quick recap and action items.
[07:54] Priya Raman: Recap: Montage wants Dedicated for production due to PCI-like requirements but may POC on Hosted. Integration points: use Python/JS SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, gateway integration with Kong/envoy, support for KMS, Prometheus export, and per-route batching configs. SE deep dive will run benchmarks with your traffic shape focusing on p99 latency and batching behavior.
[08:17] Michael Chen: That sounds right.
[08:19] Jordan Lee: Next steps: I'll send the Dedicated pricing and SKU matrix and SOC2 docs. Priya will schedule the SE deep dive and send benchmark scripts. David will provide the sample traces. Anything else?
[08:30] Sara Ortiz: Please include example code for async Python usage with our rate-limiter and the LangChain adapter.
[08:36] Priya Raman: Will do.
[08:38] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email and get the deep dive on the calendar.
[08:43] Michael Chen: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-transcriptions/word swaps expected in call export (e.g., Redwood product names sometimes abbreviated). Shared artifacts referenced: pricing-sheet.xlsx (to be sent), SOC2-package.pdf (to be sent), langchain-adapters repo link (to be sent).
